description: None of the opened sources reports a February 2021 public protest with an attendance estimate or qualitative crowd evidence. Accounts of food hardship, market restrictions, resentment, private criticism and neighbors meeting inside homes do not establish a public gathering or the 50-person threshold.
required_followup: If a contemporaneous action lead is found, seek evidence of its physical public format, simultaneous attendance, organizer and specific state-directed demand. Do not convert private complaints, workforce absences, hardship or lockdown rules into protest evidence.

description: S016 locates a hunger strike in Hyesan during a reported November 2–20, 2020 lockdown, outside the assigned month. The strike’s exact onset, duration and public setting are not reported; its profile says the interviewee escaped in 2019 while describing a 2020 event. A search-preview association with February 2021 is not confirmed in the inspected passage.
required_followup: Do not assign this account to February 2021. If the episode is researched in a separate period, resolve its chronology, public form, turnout, demand and source provenance from corroborating material.

description: S009 is a two-page Korean report for which only page one was read. Six discovered URLs remain search-only: the NCNK market report, Nautilus 2021 chronology, Daily NK COVID analysis, 2024 Human Rights Watch report, and two March lockdown reports. Their full text was not assessed.
required_followup: Review S009’s continuation and any of the six search-only sources that could add event-specific evidence, each under a fresh exact-URL receipt and contemporaneous manual scope review. Keep later-period March material separate.

description: Multiple opened reports describe a Hyesan/Samjiyon lockdown that began January 29 and was reported lifted after 18 days in mid-February. It is a state-imposed restriction, not a protest episode. No public action continuing from January or beginning in February was established. Later March search leads refer to a separate lockdown.
required_followup: If new evidence describes a protest rather than lockdown policy or private hardship, establish its own onset and determine whether it began in January, February, or March before assigning unit ownership.

description: Several contemporary reports rely on anonymous sources, interviews or accounts relayed from inside North Korea. The saved material does not establish that the RFA, Daily NK and AsiaPress reporting is independent on every lockdown detail; no protest finding depends on treating them as independent confirmations.
required_followup: Trace any later event-level claim to its underlying reporter, interview or agency; assess duplication and written origins before counting corroboration.

description: The 12 captured open-web search actions comprise 46 query expressions and 249 ordered result headers, using English and Korean plus Japanese and Chinese discovery queries, with regional, lockdown, labor, market and source-site terms. This is not a systematic archive search: North Korean domestic reporting is not openly accessible, and LexisNexis and comprehensive local newspaper collections were unavailable.
required_followup: Human review should assess North Korean and Korean-language archive coverage, source dependence and possible local events missing from the open web. The present search does not establish that no protest occurred.

description: The local May 2015 Clark–Regan codebook was consulted. The latest official event-data version and universe, additional Coding Procedure, current compatibility, and conditions for official integration remain unverified.
required_followup: Coordinator must resolve the official-baseline and additional-procedure gates before assigning official identifiers, integrating candidates or treating this dossier as approved.
